We began as a partnership with Richmond Public

Schools and we're now in 16 school divisions across Virginia. We've prepared 314 teachers in high-need schools and trained over 239 mentors. We're very proud of our graduates. They've gone on to become leaders in the school divisions. The current Richmond Teacher of the Year is one of our both graduates and mentors. Last year's was one of our mentors, the year before that was one of our graduates and so when we think about what is a teacher residency it's based on a medical residency model and we are placing we're paying people to get a degree in education and they're in a mentor teacher's classroom from the first day of teacher work week until the last day of school

for a gradual release of responsibility so over time they've gotten to see the entire school year so they feel prepared and then we're going to talk a little bit about what that um after the support as well as the framework so our product statistic that i like to say is 99 of our mentors said that being a mentor in rtr made them a more effective teacher we talk a lot about recruitment into the profession but i think we also need to focus on the retention and we know that being a leader in the classroom gives a strong reason to stay um when we we follow all of our graduates

because we've been federally funded for 12 years we make sure to do an extensive evaluation and the number one reason we do exit surveys for everyone and it's the lack of administrative support which is why we created a school leader residency and in our lab school proposal we talked about a school leader intern where a person will get a postmaster's certificate in educational leadership while working alongside rockstar school leaders like dr gordonson and so over time they'll also learn what school leadership looks like and our framework when we think about mentoring it's professional voice instructional support and social emotional learning for us it's

all about amplifying teacher joy and the love of teaching but also teaching about advocacy and leadership while at the same time feeling supported we're a training site for the new teacher center coaching model which is one of two models in the what works clearinghouse for evidence-based practices and so after they finish their residency here we provide two years of career coach support this is not evaluative it's really a way to support every um every week and then the last piece of this is as we think about the future and at code rva alone we already have

two residents that will be there working alongside rockstar teachers that are at code rva so what is code rva um we're really excited about this partnership because they've been able to serve a diverse population in 15 school divisions they've been doing this through a lottery system as well as through an extended day schedule with the six weeks for both remediation and or acceleration and so what we love is the idea that students can earn an associate's degree or up to 30 credits of dual enrollment credit and that's also where we see a huge opportunity with

a partnership with VCU as we continue to expand those opportunities and so one of the parts that we wanted to address was family engagement and I will say this is a topic near and dear to my heart this is what I wrote my dissertation on is around trust between families and teachers and as we think about communication empathy and trust we know that families want their child to have the best life that they can and for this it's all about partnerships and so from the residency side we really are trying to train future teachers to represent both the opportunities of partnerships

with families because we know that they are a student's first teacher and we also know that they know their child best and so for us as we think about how we train future teachers many people go into education for the content they might not get into education for the family side of this but we have to take both the student and the family collectively and so for us it's about the mindset of training future teachers as we think about what code rva already does what i love about this is due to their geographic area and who how many people they serve they seek to meet families busy schedules for in-person and virtual events they have a very active ptsa the raptor

school counseling advisory they live stream all of their meetings as well as send out recordings and weekly newsletters and so for us we think about how do we continue to build partnerships with families because we know that we can't meet students without meeting families too and so the other point was around increasing within the latin community what we're excited about again with partnerships with vcu is that the president of the richmond lulock is one of the professors at vcu we're very excited not just about the intentional recruitment going to the the communities, but also that we just received, we're the only ones in Virginia to receive

an Augustus F. Hawkins Center of Excellence federal grant since we last saw you all. And so what does that look like? So for us, it's to increase our multilingual ambassador program, which focuses on high schools and it's a focus on Latine students. We also are really going to put an emphasis on bilingual and multilingual learners and their families to think about the recruitment in the teaching profession, but also to get them more comfortable within the school setting. And so we're really excited that every graduate will receive a free ESOL endorsement as part of this grant. And so again, as we think about

where we go from here, we're excited to hit both of those points that were addressed last time. And the last is sustainability. As you can see with our budget, we decrease significantly from year one to year five, because for us, it's a combination of federal, state, school division, VCU, philanthropic, and corporate partnerships to ensure financial sustainability. We've been very fortunate to receive every year the General Assembly funds for the teacher residency line item, where there is a 33% cost share for school divisions. We are also looking at registered

apprenticeships through Department of Labor, and our goal is that we invest on the front end for high quality teachers so that it's for the long haul both the new teachers and veteran teachers instead of a band-aid approach of trying to help provisionally licensed teachers once they're already responsible for students and so this little bit more on the future plans of apprenticeship for us it's really the idea that you should earn while you learn everyone should be able to get paid to become a teacher and we are right now in a crisis when we think about our teacher shortage

And we want to make sure that we are allowed to have candidates have a living and be able to, again, learn, and they're also able to get a salary and benefits. And so that's where we really can build upon our proven success of the RTR model while they become employees of the school division.

So in closing, I think about this idea of these questions of what does the future of teaching, leading, and learning look like? and I stand here with immense gratitude and optimism. I'm hopeful that as we continue to explore these questions, we celebrate the successes, we learn from the challenges and move forward with a steadfast resolve to make an even greater impact in the years to come because our students deserve it.
